t: That section 2 of the joint resolution entitled “Joint resolution to authorize the Clerk of the House of Representatives to furnish certain electrical or mechanical office equipment for the use of Members, officers, and committees of the House of Representatives”, approved March 25, 1953 (2 U.S.C. 112a–1), is amended by striking out “four electric typewriters” and inserting in lieu thereof “five electric typewriters” and by striking out “five electric typewriters” and inserting in lieu thereof “six electric typewriters”.

fable.w: This section only amends the number of electric typewriters the Clerk of the House may furnish to Members, officers, and committees. Every actor involved is inside the federal government, and there is no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any outside party. The reference to Members and committees might look procedural, but it is purely internal congressional administration.

qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the number of typewriters for Members of Congress involves some form of consultation or decision-making process. There is no requirement for the government to consult with outsiders, hold public hearings, or coordinate with non-federal entities.
